content.title: Alabama’s Alexia Jayy wins ‘The Voice’: ‘No one more deserving of this honor’
content.text: Alabama’s Alexia Jayy is the new winner of “The Voice,” earning the coveted crown on Tuesday during the Season 29 finale. Jayy, a powerhouse R&B singer from Mobile County, is the second Alabama contestant to score a win on the NBC reality series during its 15-year history. She follows in the footsteps of Asher HaVon, a soul singer from Selma who took “The Voice” title in May 2024 during Season 25. Jayy, 31, is from the small town of Irvington, about 20 miles southwest of Mobile. She’s the first Black woman to win on “The Voice,” although others (including Birmingham native Jazz McKenzie) have made it to the finals. Jayy, a standout contestant throughout Season 29, was championed by her coach, Adam Levine, who called his protege “one of the most spectacular singers that I have ever heard in my life.”“I can’t believe that I’m here right now, in the final four of @nbcthevoice AND @adamlevine telling the world that I should be a household name,“ Jayy said Tuesday afternoon via Instagram. ”I am so grateful."The two shared a hug on the finale when Jayy was announced as the winner, amid a blizzard of confetti and sprays of fireworks. Alabama's Alexia Jayy shares a hug with coach Adam Levine after her Season 29 win on "The Voice." She's a powerhouse R&B singer from Mobile County.(Trae Patton/NBC)“The power of Alexia, the emotion, the way she was able to connect with all of us, that was really what made it clear that it was her night,” Levine said. “I’d say I can’t believe it, but I can,” the star added later. “There is no one that’s more deserving of this honor.” Jayy triumphed over three other contenders during the two-hour finale. Liv Ciara of St. Louis, Mo, was the runner-up. Lucas West of Rochester, N.Y., came in third, and Mikenley Brown of New Castle, Ind., took fourth place. From left, Alexia Jayy, Liv Ciara, Mikenley Brown and Lucas West were the top four finalists on Season 29 of "The Voice." Jayy won the title. Ciara was the runner-up. West took third place and Brown came in fourth.(Griffin Nagel/NBC)Three celebrity coaches — Levine, Kelly Clarkson and John Legend offered guidance to the contestants this season. West was on Team Legend; Ciara and Brown represented Team Kelly. Members of the studio audience voted to choose the winner on scene — a twist for “The Voice” this season — and the crowd included superfans and contestants from previous seasons. Series host Carson Daly waited until the final moments of the finale to announce the victor, and Jayy’s fans must have been holding their breaths for the outcome, despite her obvious talent. She kept her comments simple as the crowning moment approached. “It’s so amazing,” Jayy said, reflecting on her spot in the final four. After her win, Jayy called her family in Alabama to tell them the news. “I’m so proud of myself,” Jayy said on camera. “This means so much. I cannot believe that I just won ‘The Voice.’”Alabama's Alexia Jayy , right, celebrates with coach Adam Levine after her Season 29 win on "The Voice." She's a powerhouse R&B singer from Mobile County.(Trae Patton/NBC)Jayy was widely regarded as a frontrunner this season, turning in performances that ranged from an impressive cover of “(You Make Me Feel Like) A Natural Woman” during the Blind Auditions to a stunning rendition of “I Never Loved a Man (The Way I Love You)” for the semifinals. Another show-stopping moment was Jayy’s cover of Whitney Houston’s “You Give Good Love,” during the Knockouts. Clarkson gave Jayy a standing ovation for her performance, and predicted she’d appear at the Grammy Awards in the future. “Alexia, you are literally so good,” Clarkson said. “It is like Whitney Houston and Lauryn Hill’s voices had a baby. I want to say that I hugged you. I want to say that I knew you before, like, you’re so good. I just want to remember this moment from when you’re at the Grammys one day, and I’m like, ‘I know her.’”For Tuesday’s finals episode, Jayy chose Labelle’s “Lady Marmalade” and Adele’s “One and Only.” She earned kudos from all three coaches for her performances, plus appreciative comments from folks in the audience.“She tackled a Whitney song. She tackled Aretha, Patti LaBelle just now,” Levine said, reacting to Jayy’s cover of “Lady Marmalade.” “All these mega, mega people. The headline through all of it was you. You were what made all of these moments so special.”“I just see a star up there,” Legend said, “You carry yourself like you are supposed to be on the Grammys. Every time you deliver. You did it again today. ... All the choices she makes, she executes on it so beautifully every single time. She makes everything cooler.”Tears flowed freely, on stage and off, after Jayy offered an emotional performance of “One and Only.” “Wow! You’re like a vessel, girl, that was so good and you felt it,” Clarkson said. “That was like a therapeutic release my heart needed. Thank you. And look, I love Adele — she’s one of my favorite singers — but damn! Just promise me this, like, never cover my songs. ... Alexia crushed me in the best way possible tonight."“We’re just so proud of you, honestly,” Legend said. “You’ve just been remarkable every single time. You’ve just been a blessing to all of us, so thank you.”“You are important, man,” Levine said. “You make people reflect on their own life. When you tap into that, you make the world feel a little bit more together and communal. That’s really, really, really special. I’ve never experienced the feeling that we all just had together. Thank you for being the messenger, man. You’re unbelievable.” The four finalists performed duets with their coaches — Levine and Jay sang Maroon 5’s “Sunday Morning” — but Tuesday’s episode was less splashy than finales of the past, focusing on the contestants instead of pivoting to glitzy guest artists.“This is Alexia’s night, and I’m really proud of her,“ Clarkson said. ”Like, I’m crying again. She’s so gifted. And honestly, to see this woman that’s 31 years old and, like, where have you been?"“She was just consistently stunning, beautiful, magical,” Legend said. “I’m really happy that she won the show.” Alexia Jayy, left, competed against Bay Simpson, right, in the Knockouts round of "The Voice" during Season 29. Both singers are from Alabama. Series host Carson Daly is at center.(Griffin Nagel/NBC)Another singer from Alabama, Bay Simpson of Florence, was featured on “The Voice” this season, but he was eliminated during the Knockouts after going head-to-head with Jayy. Alabama now can claim two winners on “The Voice,” but more than 30 contestants from the state have made their marks on the show over the years, starting with Nakia Reynoso in Season 1 and continuing through Season 29.In addition to Jayy and HaVon, five singers from Alabama have competed in “The Voice” finals during previous seasons, finishing in third to sixth place. Jazz McKenzie, a soulful singer with ties to Huntsville and Birmingham, took sixth place during Season 29 in 2025. D. Smooth, an R&B singer from Birmingham, took third place during Season 23 in 2023. Dexter Roberts, a country singer from Fayette, was the third-place finisher during Season 16 in 2019. Kirk Jay, a country-soul crooner from Bay Minette, took third place on Season 15 in 2018. Red Marlow, a country singer from Rogersville, was the fourth-place finisher on Season 13 in 2017.Good to know: “The Voice” two-part finale aired at 8 p.m. CT on Monday, April 13, and Tuesday, April 14, on NBC. The series also streams on Peacock. The entire season was filmed in advance.
